Nadroga fight back to beat Kadavu 32-19 in Skipper Cup clash
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 10/10/2026 The Nadroga rugby team came from behind to beat Kadavu 32-19 in round 11 of the Skipper Cup competition at Lawaqa Park this afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 10/10/2026

The Nadroga rugby team came from behind to beat Kadavu 32-19 in round 11 of the Skipper Cup competition at Lawaqa Park this afternoon.

Kadavu gave the Stallions a run for their money, taking a 12-10 lead at half-time.

Kadavu continued to put pressure on the hosts in the second half, scoring another try to extend their lead to 19-10.

However, Nadroga fought back, scoring a try to close the gap to 19-15.

With only a few minutes remaining, the former champions regrouped and scored two more tries to take a 27-19 lead.

Kadavu refused to give up and continued to look for opportunities to break through Nadroga's defence, but the Stallions proved too strong as they secured the victory.

In other results, Tailevu defeated Taveuni 28-8 and Ba thumped Lautoka 53-22.

item.title: Seaqaqa to face Kiribati in FMF IDC Premier Division final
item.description: Mohammed Feroz , Priya Nand · 10/10/2026 Seaqaqa FC will face the Kiribati National Team in the 86th FMF Inter-District Championship Premier Division final tomorrow after staging an impressive comeback to beat Tavua FC 3-1 in the semi-final.
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Feroz , Priya Nand · 10/10/2026

Seaqaqa FC will face the Kiribati National Team in the 86th FMF Inter-District Championship Premier Division final tomorrow after staging an impressive comeback to beat Tavua FC 3-1 in the semi-final.

Seaqaqa were trailing 1-0 at half-time but came back strongly in the second half, scoring three goals to secure their place in the final.

Seaqaqa coach Mohammed Imran says his players showed determination and refused to give up despite being behind at the break.

Imran says the team remained hopeful and came out firing in the second half to score three goals and seal the win.

He thanked the players and supporters for their efforts and encouragement, saying their support gave the team extra motivation.

He says the team will now focus on preparing for tomorrow's final.

Kiribati booked their place in the final after defeating the Fiji Under-17 national team 3-1 in the second semi-final at Buckhurst Park.

The Premier Division final will kick off at 12pm tomorrow at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Meanwhile, Shah Group of Companies Dreketi FC will face Bua FC in the Senior Division final at 9.30am tomorrow after both teams secured victories in their respective semi-finals.

In other matches, the Super Premier Division semi-final between defending champions Stratum/Lincoln Rewa FC and Vantex Solutions Navua FC is currently underway at HFC Bank Stadium , while Dayals Steel Ba FC will take on Extra Supermarket Labasa FC at 5pm.

The Super Premier Division final is scheduled for 3pm tomorrow at HFC Bank Stadium.
